verdict.rationale: Kick's own docs say it automatically categorizes synced transactions (about 97% on the first pass), states that it "learns from your changes," leaves low-confidence items for manual review, and logs AI categorization in the audit trail. User-defined Rules can override AI categorization. However, the learn-from-corrections mechanism is a single unelaborated claim. Categorization of statement or CSV imports specifically, as opposed to bank-feed syncs, is only implied, and the AI applies categories directly rather than surfacing reviewable suggestions. Missing for 10: documented detail on how corrections feed back into future categorization, explicit confirmation that AI categorization runs on Universal Importer (PDF/CSV) imports, a suggestion/review workflow rather than auto-application, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can get automatic categorization suggestions for imported transactions that learn from my corrections

citations.quote: Kick automatically categorizes your transactions and learns from your changes.
the AI categorizes approximately 97% of them on the first pass - things like meals, software subscriptions, payroll, rent, and revenue.
When Kick's confidence is low, the transaction is left uncategorized for you to review manually
Every transaction in Kick comes from a bank feed or an import.
automated categorization, transfer matching, and other AI actions are logged under the relevant Kick agent
